# Github (12 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /profile | `handle` | 1 | Get a GitHub user profile |
| /repo | `url` | 1 | Get a GitHub repository |
| /profile/repos | `handle` | 1 | List a GitHub user's repositories |
| /repo/readme | `url` | 1 | Get a repository's README |
| /repo/releases | `url` | 1 | List a repository's releases |
| /repo/issues | `url` | 1 | List a repository's issues (and PRs) |
| /issue | `url` | 1 | Get a single issue or pull request |
| /issue/comments | `url` | 1 | Get comments on an issue or pull request |
| /search | `query` | 1 | Search GitHub issues and pull requests |
| /repo/top-issues | `url` | 5 | Top feature request and top complaint for a repository |
| /repo/dossier | `url` | 5 | Full project dossier for a repository |
| /user/profile-velocity | `handle` | 10 | User contribution velocity dossier |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /profile — 1cr

Returns public profile information for a GitHub user — login, name, avatar, bio, follower / following / public-repos counts, and account-creation date — mapped to the unified Author schema. `author.likes_count` surfaces `public_gists` (a creation-count analog); `author.verified` surfaces the rare `site_admin` flag (true only for GitHub staff accounts).

**Parameters**

- `handle`: GitHub username — 1–39 chars, alphanumeric + non-consecutive hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/profile?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /repo — 1cr

Returns repository metadata — full_name, description, stars, forks, open issues, watchers, language, and creation date — mapped to the unified Author schema. A repo is a follow-able creator-like entity in this API: stars map to `author.followers`, watchers (subscribers) to `author.likes_count`, forks to `author.following`. Use `/v1/github/repo/readme`, `/v1/github/repo/releases`, and `/v1/github/repo/issues` for richer per-repo data.

**Parameters**

- `url`: GitHub repo URL — `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/repo?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /profile/repos — 1cr

Returns the public repositories owned by the user under `data.items[]` — each entry includes `id`, `name`, `full_name`, `description`, `language`, `stargazers_count`, `forks_count`, `created_at`, and `pushed_at`. Sortable by `created`, `updated`, `pushed`, or `full_name`. Use `/v1/github/repo` for a single richer repo dossier.

**Parameters**

- `handle`: GitHub username.
- `type` *(optional)*: Filter — `all`, `owner`, or `member`. Defaults to `owner`.
- `sort` *(optional)*: Sort field — `created`, `updated`, `pushed`, or `full_name`. Defaults to `full_name`.
- `direction` *(optional)*: `asc` or `desc`. Defaults to `asc` for full_name, `desc` otherwise.
- `per_page` *(optional)*: Repos per page (1–100). Defaults to 30. Native upstream page-size param. Send the universal `limit` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `page` *(optional)*: 1-indexed page number for pagination. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Universal page size. The API maps it to this endpoint's native `per_page`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/profile/repos?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /repo/readme — 1cr

Returns the repository's README in raw form (the file contents, not base64-wrapped). The fetcher sets `Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json` so the response body is the actual file. Useful for content discovery and AI-grounding workflows.

**Parameters**

- `url`: GitHub repo URL — `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/repo/readme?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /repo/releases — 1cr

Returns the most recent releases for the repository under `data.items[]` — each entry includes `tag_name`, `name`, `body` (markdown release notes), `published_at`, `prerelease`, and `assets[]`. Sorted newest-first by upstream default.

**Parameters**

- `url`: GitHub repo URL — `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}`.
- `per_page` *(optional)*: Releases per page (1–100). Defaults to 30. Native upstream page-size param. Send the universal `limit` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `page` *(optional)*: 1-indexed page number. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Universal page size. The API maps it to this endpoint's native `per_page`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/repo/releases?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /repo/issues — 1cr

Returns issues for the repository under `data.items[]`. NOTE: GitHub treats pull requests as issues for this endpoint — every PR also appears here, distinguishable by the presence of a `pull_request` field on the item. Filter by `state`, comma-separated `labels`, sort by `created`/`updated`/`comments`, and paginate with `per_page`/`page`. `since` accepts an ISO 8601 timestamp.

**Parameters**

- `url`: GitHub repo URL — `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}`.
- `type` *(optional)*: Filter the unified issues+PRs list — `issue` returns only issues, `pr` returns only pull requests, `all` (default) returns both. Each item also carries `post.ext.type` (`issue`/`pull_request`).
- `state` *(optional)*: `open`, `closed`, or `all`. Defaults to `open`.
- `labels` *(optional)*: Comma-separated label names (e.g. `bug,help wanted`).
- `sort` *(optional)*: `created`, `updated`, or `comments`. Defaults to `created`.
- `direction` *(optional)*: `asc` or `desc`. Defaults to `desc`.
- `since` *(optional)*: Only issues updated at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.
- `per_page` *(optional)*: Issues per page (1–100). Defaults to 30. Native upstream page-size param. Send the universal `limit` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `page` *(optional)*: 1-indexed page number. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Universal page size. The API maps it to this endpoint's native `per_page`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/repo/issues?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /issue — 1cr

Returns full metadata for an issue or PR — title, body, author, labels, state, reactions, comments count, and timestamps — mapped to the unified Post schema. Pass either an `/issues/N` or `/pull/N` URL; GitHub's API treats them interchangeably under `/issues/N`. Use `/v1/github/issue/comments` for the discussion thread.

**Parameters**

- `url`: GitHub HTML URL — `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}` or `/pull/{n}`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/issue?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /issue/comments — 1cr

Returns comments under `data.items[]` — each entry includes `id`, `user.login`, `body`, `reactions.total_count`, and `created_at`. Pass either an `/issues/N` or `/pull/N` URL; both resolve to the same comment thread on GitHub's API. Comments are returned in ascending `created_at` order (GitHub does not support re-sorting a single issue's comments).

**Parameters**

- `url`: GitHub HTML URL of the issue or PR.
- `since` *(optional)*: Only comments updated at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.
- `per_page` *(optional)*: Comments per page (1–100). Defaults to 30. Native upstream page-size param. Send the universal `limit` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `page` *(optional)*: 1-indexed page number. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Universal page size. The API maps it to this endpoint's native `per_page`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/issue/comments?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /search — 1cr

Searches issues and PRs across all of GitHub via the `/search/issues` endpoint. Supports GitHub's full search syntax — qualifiers like `repo:owner/name`, `is:issue`, `is:pr`, `is:open`, `label:bug`, `created:>2026-01-01`, `author:username`, `comments:>10`. Sort by `reactions`, `comments`, `created`, or `updated`. Results land under `data.items[]` with `total_count` and `incomplete_results` siblings. Rate-limited to 30 req/min per token.

**Parameters**

- `query`: GitHub search query (uses GitHub's qualifier syntax — see https://docs.github.com/en/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-issues-and-pull-requests).
- `sort` *(optional)*: Sort field — `reactions`, `comments`, `created`, `updated`. Defaults to best-match relevance.
- `order` *(optional)*: `asc` or `desc`. Defaults to `desc`.
- `per_page` *(optional)*: Results per page (1–100). Defaults to 30. Native upstream page-size param. Send the universal `limit` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `page` *(optional)*: 1-indexed page number. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Universal page size. The API maps it to this endpoint's native `per_page`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /repo/top-issues — 5cr

Composite endpoint — runs two `/search/issues` queries in parallel: `top_feature_request` (issues with `enhancement` label, sorted by reactions; falls back to top open issue by reactions if no label exists) and `top_complaint` (most-discussed open issue, sorted by comments). Returns `{ top_feature_request, top_complaint }`. 5 credits per call.

**Parameters**

- `url`: GitHub repo URL — `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/repo/top-issues?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /repo/dossier — 5cr

Composite endpoint — fetches repo metadata, README excerpt, latest 3 releases, top feature request, and top complaint in parallel and returns a structured dossier `{ info, readme, releases, top_issues }`. Useful for AI-grounding workflows where a single call should return everything you'd need to summarise a project. 5 credits per call.

**Parameters**

- `url`: GitHub repo URL — `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/repo/dossier?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /user/profile-velocity — 10cr

Composite endpoint — combines a `/search/issues` PR-velocity query (total + merged), the user's own repo list, and parallel per-repo enrichment (stars + releases for external repos; README + releases + top-issues for own repos) into a structured contribution dossier `{ velocity, contributed_repos[], own_repos[] }`. The `depth` param controls fan-out width: `quick` enriches up to 5 external + 3 own repos, `default` 10 + 5, `deep` 15 + 5. 10 credits per call.

**Parameters**

- `handle`: GitHub username.
- `depth` *(optional)*: `quick`, `default`, or `deep`. Defaults to `default`. Trades off upstream calls vs. dossier richness.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/github/user/profile-velocity?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a GitHub endpoint

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| A user, a repo, their repos | `/profile` · `/repo` · `/profile/repos` | 1 |
| README, releases, issues | `/repo/readme` · `/repo/releases` · `/repo/issues` | 1 |
| One issue or PR, and its comments | `/issue` · `/issue/comments` | 1 |
| Search issues and PRs | `/search` | 1 |
| **Top feature request + top complaint** | `/repo/top-issues` | 5 |
| A full project dossier | `/repo/dossier` | 5 |
| A user's contribution velocity | `/user/profile-velocity` | **10** |

### `/repo/top-issues` is product research, not code research

At 5cr it returns the single most-wanted feature and the loudest complaint for a repo. For any
developer-tool niche that is a distilled voice-of-customer read — the same job
`prism/audience-questions` does for 30cr, scoped to one project.

The 1cr endpoints do the raw work: `/repo/issues` plus `/issue/comments` gets you there for
less if you are willing to read. Pay for `/repo/top-issues` when you want the verdict rather
than the material, and `/repo/dossier` (5cr) when you want releases, issue load and the
request/complaint pair rolled together.

For a whole organisation rather than one repo, `prism/org-radar` (26cr) expands an org's top
repos into dossiers and rolls them up. For how a launch landed across Hacker News and dev
blogs, `prism/launch-echo` (20cr) or `prism/devtool-pulse` (20cr).

## Field Maps


- `profile` → `Author` via the `github-author` field map (followers, following, public_repos → likes_count, etc.). Includes computed fields under `data.computed`.
- `repo` → `Author` via the `github-repo` field map (stargazers_count → followers, forks_count → following, subscribers_count → likes_count). Includes computed fields.
- `issue` → `Post` via the `github-post` field map (title → content.text, reactions.total_count → engagement.likes, comments → engagement.comments).
- All other endpoints are passthrough — `repo/readme` returns the raw markdown string, the rest pass GitHub's native JSON.
- Use `?format=raw` to bypass field-mapping on the three field-mapped endpoints.

## Composite endpoints


The 3 composite endpoints fan out multiple GitHub calls server-side and fold the results into a single dossier:

- **`repo/top-issues`** (~3 calls) — `{ top_feature_request, top_complaint }`. Either can be `null`. If both are null, returns 404 with credit refunded.
- **`repo/dossier`** (~5 calls in parallel) — `{ info, readme, releases, top_issues }`. The `info` call is critical (404 → refund); other enrichments degrade gracefully.
- **`user/profile-velocity`** (~5–15 calls) — `{ velocity, contributed_repos, own_repos }`. Three depth modes via the `depth` optional param: `quick` (3 own + 5 external), `default` (5 + 10), `deep` (5 + 15). `deep` can take 2–3 seconds wall-clock.

## Rate limits


The shared service token caps at 5,000 req/hr for general endpoints and 30 req/min for search. Cache TTLs (profile 15min, post 10min, comments 5min, search 2min, analytics 30min) absorb most of it. Cache hits and 4xx/5xx refunds keep customers off the hook when the bucket is squeezed.
